in_text_mentions: Facial weakness, along with other characteristic features of DM1, can contribute to an appearance that may seem tired or expressionless. The facial signs vary from subtle, sometimes only acknowledged as sign of the disease after a patient is diagnosed, to severe myopathic facies. Typical features include bilateral ptosis, difficulty closing the eyes completely, and frontal balding in men. Temporal wasting gives rise to a long, thin facial contour (Fig. 1) [12].

in_text_mentions: The correlations between the muscle MRI findings and the histopathological findings of biopsy specimens of the muscle were examined in patients 4, 7, and 15. In patients 7 and 15, T1-weighted high-intensity signals on MRI of the biceps muscle were associated with characteristic pathological findings, such as central nuclei, variable ranges of fiber size, and fatty degeneration (Fig 4). In contrast, the biceps muscle in patient 4, associated with no high-intensity signals on MRI, showed mild pathological findings without fatty degeneration (data not shown).

in_text_mentions: Cranial computertomography showed numerous periventricular hypodense lesions without signs of acute cerebral infarction. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed twice revealing general brain atrophy and multiple white matter lesions in all cerebral lobes, including the temporal region (Figures 1 and 2). No gadolinium enhancement and no abnormalities in diffusion weighted images (DWI) were found. No progression of the white matter lesions was detected from June to October on MRI scans.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: Axial FLAIR MRI shows pontine and subcortical signal alterations consistent with DM1 white matter disease. B: Coronal T2 MRI demonstrates bilateral anterior temporal white matter hyperintensities, a hallmark finding in DM1. C: Axial DWI MRI shows pontine hyperintensity consistent with T2 shine-through from demyelination. D: Axial ADC MRI shows no hypointense signal in the pons, ruling out acute infarction and supporting T2 shine-through. E: Axial FLAIR MRI demonstrates multiple white matter hyperintensities in cerebellar and subcortical regions. F: Axial FLAIR MRI shows additional white matter hyperintensities in the temporal region. G: Sagittal T2 MRI of the cervical spine included in the radiological demonstration; arrowhead points to upper spinal region. H: Axial MRI highlights muscular atrophy in the lower extremity consistent with DM1 myopathy.

The in parallel performed trancutaneous canpnography over a period of 10,3 hours revealed a minimum pCO2 of 45 mmHg, median of 52 mmHg, maximum of 61 mmHg with 9 events of a pCO2 > 50 mmHg of a duration of mo

to 800 CTG-repeats. The MRI of our patient revealed pontine signal alterations in FLAIR, T2 and DWI weighted images, while the ADC weighted images showed no hypointense signal in the pontine region (Fig. 1). The elevated signal in DWI weighted images is thus a T2 shine-through and might be explained by demyelination. There is no sign of an acute infarction. This, again, fits well with the neuropathology of DM1, of which demyelination is a key feature [5]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial FLAIR MRI from a patient with confirmed myotonic dystrophy type 1; caption and in-text explicitly attribute the bilateral anterior temporal white matter hyperintensity to DM1, a classic and characteristic MRI finding of the disease. Arrows annotate the lesions. B: Coronal T2-weighted MRI from the same myotonic dystrophy type 1 patient; caption and in-text confirm the temporal lobe white matter hyperintensity is a manifestation of DM1, a recognized classic finding. Arrow annotates the lesion.

panels.figure_caption: MRI of myotonic dystrophy type 1. A: Axial FLAIR sequence showing a hyperintense signal in the white matter of the temporal lobes. B: Coronal T2-weighted sequence showing an area of hyperintense signal in the white matter of the temporal lobes. There was no restricted diffusion on DWI (not shown).
in_text_mentions: On MRI, the alterations caused by myotonic dystrophy type 1 manifest as supratentorial lesions of the white matter and mild cortical atrophy without restricted diffusion on DWI. Although the frontal lobes are most commonly affected, alterations can also occur in the temporo-insular region, which does not occur in myotonic dystrophy type 2. Although MRI is essential for the assessment of these patients, the definitive diagnosis is made by means of genetic testing(8). Figure 7 shows a case of myotonic dystrophy type 1.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (2a, 2b). 2a: Axial FLAIR brain MRI of Patient A with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (disease-focused article title) showing periventricular white matter hyperintensity and multiple subcortical white matter hyperintensities with partial confluence. The in-text localizes the subcortical lesions to the frontal, parietal and anteromedial temporal lobes, supporting the DM1 anterior temporal white matter hyperintensity finding. Real patient radiology image, not a diagram, control or other disease. 2b: Axial FLAIR brain MRI of the same DM1 patient showing white matter hyperintensity posterior and superior to the trigone, a DM1 white matter change. The vocabulary anterior-temporal finding is not localized to this panel, so the peritrigonal lesion is recorded as a proposed finding rather than a vocabulary finding. Real patient radiology image.

A: Case 1 is one of the two adult siblings with DM1 in the article title; the full-body appearance panel shows textbook cranial/neck DM1 features, supported by the in-text note that he was thin. H&E staining shows interstitial fibrosis (light pink regions) between cardiomyocytes as well as fatty infiltration (clear circumscribed areas in the middle of the tissue indicative of fat droplets). Gamori-trichrome staining highlights collagen (blue). Oil Red O staining detects lipids (red). Perilipin immunofluorescence (Perilipin-IF) (green) detects perilipin, a surface marker on fat droplets. Scale bar is 200 µm for above row and 100 µm for bottom row.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (BASELINE, FOLLOW-UP). BASELINE: Baseline axial chest MRI in 20-year-old male DM1 patient P6 showing pectoralis minor annotated by open arrowhead; caption states STIR-independent atrophy-progression of pectoralis minor. Article is DM1 longitudinal muscle MRI study. No vocabulary finding_key covers pectoral/upper-trunk atrophy on MRI, so coded as proposed finding. FOLLOW-UP: Follow-up axial chest MRI after 37 months in same DM1 patient P6 showing progressive pectoralis minor atrophy annotated by solid arrowhead; caption and in-text state atrophy progression in upper body without STIR positivity. No vocabulary finding_key covers this site, so coded as proposed finding.
